resources.string: Collects the technical information needed to port LibreHU to another head unit, ROM, MCU, CAN box or car. Read only: nothing on the unit is changed.
Looking for root (the ROM\'s own su, then the root managers)…
No root: the report is collected without it (fewer details, no partition images, no hardware scan).
KernelSU / KernelSU Next / APatch: allow LibreHU Helper in the manager\'s Superuser list, then search again. Magisk / SuperSU: answer the prompt.
The sections to collect. Those using root also work without it, with less.
Removes serial numbers, IMEI, Wi-Fi / Bluetooth addresses, Android ID and GPS positions from the text files.
Plug in a USB key if you want (not required), then choose the folder where the zip report is written.
App\'s folder: Android/data/org.librehu.helper/files/diag (also used when the ROM has no folder picker).
Build, real Android version, properties, kernel line, partitions, fstab, mounts, services, HALs, processes, apps, maker\'s apps
logcat (every buffer with root), kernel log, previous boot, crashes and tombstones
Kernel config, modules, device tree (text and .dtb), input devices and key layouts, I²C / USB / PCI devices, serial ports, sound, video, GPIO, CPU, display, audio / input / Bluetooth services
Listing and small text files of /jancar, /oem, /custom… (CAN box, keys, touch, car settings), audio policy, media codecs, build.prop
I²C buses, Apple MFi chip, UART traffic, MCU and CAN box protocols with draft LibreHU-service profiles. Off by default: it reads the hardware.
boot, recovery, dtbo, vbmeta… (root), for a TWRP or kernel port. Large: off by default.
What this head unit has, check by check, with what may cause trouble and what to try.
Looks portable: no blocking point found.
Portable with work: see the points in yellow.
Blocking point found: see the points in red.
The LibreHU apps need Android 9 at least (minSdk 28).
LibreHU-service ships native code for arm64-v8a only: it would have to be built for this architecture.
%1$s: same family as the reference UJC201, the closest drivers and paths.
The Autochips (ATC) functions will be missing; MCU, CAN and audio depend on the board.
Longer port: FM driver, audio chip and ATC functions to adapt. The full report and the hardware scan are essential.
Several LibreHU-service functions go through root (raw touch, touch calibration, system settings): install KernelSU Next or Magisk, then search again.

Two programs on one serial port steal each other\'s frames: LibreHU-service refuses to drive the hardware while Jancar\'s ivi-services is enabled. Same idea here: disable the maker\'s service once LibreHU-service is set up (Guides tab).
No MCU / CAN service recognised among the %1$d maker\'s apps found.
Without root, /dev cannot be listed on some ROMs: try again with root.
Usually the MCU or the CAN box, held by the maker\'s service; the hardware scan reads it without changing its speed.
Says %1$s, the SDK level says %2$s: faked by the ROM.
Apps reading the Android version are misled; rely on the SDK level.
To change /system or flash a recovery, disable dm-verity yourself first (fastboot --disable-verity flash vbmeta vbmeta.img): this app never does it.
The LibreHU apps are laid out for 1280 × 720 at 160 dpi (UJC201) or larger; below, some screens may be cramped.
%1$d MB free (a full dump goes to a USB key)
LibreHU-service does not see the MCU: disable the maker\'s service holding the port (Hardware tab: \"held by\"), check the port and speed of the MCU profile, restart the link.
Steering wheel keys do nothing: capture a key (Hardware tab) to see whether it comes through the MCU, the CAN box or the kernel, then choose the matching CAN box protocol in LibreHU-service.
No sound: the audio chip and its routing differ from one model to the next (BD37534 on the UJC201); join sound.txt and audio-hal.txt of the report for the port.
Bluetooth / phone: the maker\'s Bluetooth app may keep the module; disable it only once LibreHU Téléphone is installed.
The unit misbehaves after disabling an app: enable it again with adb shell pm enable <package>; a factory reset also enables every disabled app.
Sleep / wake: the maker\'s service usually handles the ignition (ACC); without it, LibreHU-service does it (acc input of the MCU profile).

Read only: I²C buses probed with reads (like i2cdetect -r), serial ports read without sending anything, at their current speed; a free port is also tried at the usual speeds. During a capture, the maker\'s service may miss a few bytes. Root is needed for most scans.
Also change the speed of used ports
For ports held by the maker\'s service: may disturb the MCU or the CAN box while the capture lasts.
No protocol recognised (root, or the device is silent: turn the ignition on, press a key during the scan).
Draft MCU profiles (LibreHU-service format) are in the report, Hardware scan section (scan/draft-profiles.json).
After a scan: 3 s without touching anything, then 5 s during which you press ONE key (wheel or front panel). Frames seen only during the press are the key\'s; kernel events cover wired keys.

Found without a fixed list: known prefixes (Jancar, Autochips, MediaTek, FYT com.syu, Microntek) and clues (system app neither AOSP nor Google, place, system uid, name, serial port held). The APKs (and their odex / vdex) go into a zip: keep it before disabling anything.

Copy of the partitions, each in its own zip (a FAT32 USB key takes files of 4 GB at most). Never: userdata (personal data), nvram, nvdata, nvcfg, proinfo, persist, metazone, protect, otp, frp (data of this unit only: IMEI, MAC, calibration). Nothing is written to the unit.
%1$s base: a scatter file can be used.
Choose the firmware\'s scatter file (MTxxxx_Android_scatter.txt) to add the partitions without a by-name link (preloader…), read at their address.

On the stock head unit, a maker\'s service holds the MCU, the CAN box, the radio, Bluetooth… LibreHU-service replaces it, but two programs on one serial port steal each other\'s frames: LibreHU-service refuses to drive the hardware while Jancar\'s ivi-services is enabled. So the maker\'s apps are disabled once LibreHU is installed and set up.
LibreHU Helper disables nothing itself: it gives the commands.
Back up the maker\'s APKs first (Maker\'s APKs tab) and make a report.
Install and set up the LibreHU apps (LibreHU Apps).
Disable one app at a time, the MCU / CAN service first, then reboot and check.
Write down what was disabled, to go back if needed.
With USB debugging (developer options) and adb on a computer. disable-user disables the app for user 0 without root; it stays installed.
Some head unit ROMs have no adb over USB: try adb over the network if the ROM offers it, or the root way.
On the unit (terminal) or through adb shell, with root:
A factory reset also enables every disabled app.
No maker\'s app with a known role (MCU, CAN, Bluetooth, radio…) was found.
Press Home and choose LibreHU Launcher, \"Always\"; or Settings → Apps → Default apps → Home app. Then disable the maker\'s launcher if needed.
pm commands: developer.android.com/tools/adb (pm disable-user, enable, list packages).
